title: A common step near 2009 makes NDBC buoy winter wave heights fall 2-3% per decade faster than altimetry and a wave hindcast; the corrected Hawaii decrease is about 1.5% per decade
abstract: We tested a campaign result that winter (November to March) significant wave height (Hs) at Hawaii NDBC buoys decreased 3.1% per decade in 1985-2025 and that no US region increased. We used two sources that do not use buoy wave data: ESA Sea State CCI v4.0 L4 altimetry (3 x 3 degree boxes at 47 buoys, winters 1993-2023) and the Ifremer WAVEWATCH III hindcast GLOB-30M_LOPS_2025 with ERA5 winds (3-hourly at 13 buoys, 1992-2025). We compared the published buoy winter values with each source by fixed-effects composites, ONI-adjusted trends, difference series and a common step scan. At Hawaii in 1993-2023 the buoys gave -3.95% per decade (95% CI -5.26 to -2.62), altimetry -1.06% (-2.04 to -0.08) and the hindcast -1.95% (-3.59 to -0.29); altimetry minus hindcast was +0.91% (-0.32 to +2.16). Buoy minus altimetry at all 47 buoys fits one common step better than a linear drift (BIC lower by 29.5): first winter 2010 (bootstrap 2007-2013), step -4.4% (-5.6 to -3.4); 42 of 47 buoys drift negative. Buoy minus hindcast gives the same step (winter 2009, -4.2%) at all 13 buoys, also in the 95th percentile. Altimetry minus hindcast has no clear common drift or step. Removal of the network step changes the published 1985-2025 Hawaii trend from -3.0% to -1.5% per decade (-2.2 to -0.8) and moves the other regions to near zero or small increases. In the hindcast, the Hawaii decrease is North Pacific swell (-2.4% per decade), not local wind sea. Thus the Hawaii decrease is real in sign but about half as large, and a network-wide NDBC change near 2009 biases buoy trends negative. Limitations: the cause of the step is not identified; the references disagree by up to 2% per decade in the Gulf of Mexico and Southeast Atlantic and by about 1% per decade in the Pacific; the hindcast covers only 13 buoys; altimetry uses monthly 1-degree means.

citations.reason: We use its published per-station winter buoy values and regional composites and test its main result. Independent altimetry and a hindcast confirm the sign of the Hawaii winter Hs decrease but give about half the size; a common network step near 2009, which its neighbour test could not see, causes the rest and the absence of regional increases.
Its corrected KIP microseism trend is negative at Hawaii; our altimetry and hindcast also give a negative Hawaii winter trend.
